question.text: In the context of futures, what does 'zero-sum game' mean?

answer.text: The total profit earned by one party equals the total loss incurred by the other party
The net position of all traders is always zero
The futures price always equals the spot price
The initial investment in futures is zero

explanation.text: The Logic: A futures trade is a zero-sum equation: the profit of one trader is exactly equal to the loss of the opposite trader. Long and short futures positions are equal in open interest, so gains on one side correspond rupee-for-rupee with losses on the other. The Trap: Net position being zero refers to OI accounting, not to P&L symmetry. Futures prices need not equal spot (basis exists), and initial margins are not zero - the zero-sum idea is purely about P&L. Note: The symmetry is between long and short futures only; it does not extend to other product structures unless separately established.
